title: Ordered localization coordinates identify the scalar-extended tensor Cech complex
statement: Let (C,J,O) be a small commutative ringed site, A its global ring and T its explicit scalar extension [def-weil-pbc-global-section-scalar-extension]. Fix r global sections f. Let K be an augmented A-module complex with actual ordered localization coordinates as in [def-weil-pbc-ring-complex-cech-data]: K^0 is A, K^(q+1) is the product of A localized at the product f(t i) over increasing t:Fin(q+1) into Fin r, negative terms are zero, the differential is the alternating sum of A-algebra localization maps (the initial differential is the diagonal localization map), and the augmentation is the degree-zero identification. Then the tensor extended Cech complex [def-weil-pbc-ringed-extended-cech] is isomorphic as an augmented complex to T(K). No replacement complex P, K-flat hypothesis or derived-category comparison is required.

source.place: Tags 099D(c),(d), 099E, final paragraph; Tag 0996 for the finite tensor localization model

proof.text: Use the ordered localization coordinates of the actual ring tensor complex. Lift the degree-zero and positive-degree coordinate equivalences composed with the inverse of the supplied equivalences to isomorphisms of one-point module sheaves; lift negative degrees using their zero objects. The supplied face maps equal the ring tensor face maps by uniqueness of algebra maps out of a localization. Substituting the first and later differential equations proves the cochain equations and hence constructs an isomorphism from the ring tensor complex to K.

The two degree-zero augmentation equations show that this isomorphism commutes with augmentation after postcomposition with the single-complex degree-zero isomorphism; cancel it. In all nonzero degrees the target is zero. Map this augmented isomorphism through the actual additive global scalar-extension functor. Compose it with the tensor base-change comparison and use functoriality of composition to obtain exactly the displayed augmentation equation.

theorem ringFamilyGlobalExtension_ordered_iso
    {C : Type u} [SmallCategory C] {J : GrothendieckTopology C}
    (O : Sheaf J CommRingCat.{u})
    (r : ℕ) (f : Fin r → (O.obj ⋙ forget CommRingCat).sections)
    (K : CochainComplex (RingSiteModules (ringFamilyGlobalRing O)) ℤ)
    (a : K ⟶ ringComplexSingle (ringFamilyGlobalRing O))
    (e₀ : (K.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) ≃ₗ[ringFamilyGlobalRing O]
      ringFamilyGlobalRing O)
    (e : ∀ q : ℕ, (K.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)
      ≃ₗ[ringFamilyGlobalRing O]
        ((t : Fin (q + 1) ↪o Fin r) →
          Localization.Away (∏ i, ringFamilyGlobalList O r f (t i))))
    (l : ∀ (q : ℕ) (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r) (j : Fin (q + 2)),
      Localization.Away (∏ i, ringFamilyGlobalList O r f (t (Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j i)))
        →ₐ[ringFamilyGlobalRing O]
          Localization.Away (∏ i, ringFamilyGlobalList O r f (t i)))
    (hneg : ∀ n : ℤ, n < 0 → CategoryTheory.Limits.IsZero (K.X n))
    (hd₀ : ∀ (x : (K.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩)) (t : Fin 1 ↪o Fin r),
      e 0 ((K.d 0 1).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
        algebraMap (ringFamilyGlobalRing O)
          (Localization.Away (∏ i, ringFamilyGlobalList O r f (t i))) (e₀ x))
    (hd : ∀ (q : ℕ) (x : (K.X ((q : ℤ) + 1)).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩))
      (t : Fin (q + 2) ↪o Fin r),
      e (q + 1) ((K.d ((q : ℤ) + 1) ((q : ℤ) + 2)).val.app (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩) x) t =
        ∑ j : Fin (q + 2), (-1 : ℤ) ^ j.val •
          l q t j (e q x ((Fin.succAboveOrderEmb j).trans t)))
    (ha : ∀ x : (K.X 0).val.obj (op ⟨PUnit.unit⟩),
      ringComplexAugmentationValue a x = e₀ x) :
    ∃ e : (ringedExtendedCech O r f).1 ≅ ringFamilyGlobalExtensionComplex O K,
      e.hom ≫ ringFamilyGlobalExtensionAugmentation O a = (ringedExtendedCech O r f).2
